paper.title_en: Efficient Analysis of Numerous Galactic Compact Binaries via the Free-bin Scheme
paper.abstract_en: Global analysis of Galactic compact binaries (GCBs) for space-based gravitational-wave detectors is computationally demanding in the high-frequency region (above $\sim$10 mHz), where resolvable signals are sparse but frequency samples are numerous. We propose a free-bin scheme that evaluates the nontrivial likelihood only in movable frequency windows centered on sampled signal frequencies. The method preserves the joint-likelihood structure by replacing only the signal-containing regions of a precomputed null likelihood, and avoids the fixed-bin edge effect by construction because the windows follow the sampled frequencies. In a simulated TianQin dataset containing 193 GCBs, 192 injected sources are recovered with waveform fitting factors above 0.99. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the free-bin and conventional full-band likelihood implementations yield identical results when the same finite-length local waveforms and numerical settings are used. Computational benchmarks show that the acceleration is primarily controlled by the fraction of the frequency domain covered by the merged signal windows and decreases as this coverage increases.
